entries.why: THE-336 owns this file. Both Firestore writes moved off updateDoc, which requires the document to exist and rejected 'not-found' on a member whose users doc was never created, and onto writeUserDoc, which updates an existing document and creates a COMPLETE one when it is missing. The hand-written error banner was replaced with ui/alert behind a saveState machine, which removed the file's three bare hex literals and gave a refused write a role="alert" it never had.

THE-336 owns this file. It carried the root cause: five Firestore call sites ending in handleFirestoreError(...) followed by a bare return, and handleFirestoreError logs and returns rather than throwing. A refused create was therefore swallowed, leaving an Auth user with no users document and nothing on screen. Both creating writes now surface the failure; the two consent refreshes no longer abort the set-claims call after them.
